verses.zh: （大卫上行之诗。）以色列人要说：若不是耶和华帮助我们，
verses.en: A song of ascents;[NOTE:1] by David.“If the Lord had not been on our side”—let Israel say this.—
notes: Psalm 124. Israel acknowledges that the Lord delivered them from certain disaster.

verses.zh: 若不是耶和华帮助我们，当人起来攻击我们、
verses.en: if the Lord had not been on our side,when men attacked us,[NOTE:1]
notes: The precise significance of this title, which appears in Pss 120-134, is unclear. Perhaps worshipers recited these psalms when they ascended the road to Jerusalem to celebrate annual religious festivals. For a discussion of their background see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 219-21.

verses.zh: 向我们发怒的时候，就把我们活活地吞了。
verses.en: they would have swallowed us alive,when their anger raged against us.

verses.zh: 那时，波涛必漫过我们，河水必淹没我们，
verses.en: The water would have overpowered us;the current[NOTE:1] would have overwhelmed[NOTE:2] us.[NOTE:3]
The raging waterwould have overwhelmed us.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “our being.” The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) with a pronominal suffix is often equivalent to a pronoun, especially in poetry (see BDB 660 s.v. נֶפֶשׁ 4.a).

verses.zh: 耶和华是应当称颂的！他没有把我们当野食交给他们吞吃（原文是牙齿）。
verses.en: The Lord deserves praise,[NOTE:1] for[NOTE:2] he did not hand us over as prey to their teeth.
notes: Heb “then they would have passed over our being, the raging waters.”

verses.zh: 我们好像雀鸟，从捕鸟人的网罗里逃脱；网罗破裂，我们逃脱了。
verses.en: We escaped with our lives,[NOTE:1] like a bird from a hunter’s snare.The snare broke, and we escaped.

verses.zh: 我们得帮助，是在乎倚靠造天地之耶和华的名。
verses.en: Our deliverer is the Lord,[NOTE:1] the Creator[NOTE:2] of heaven and earth.
notes: Heb “our help [is] in the name of the Lord.”

"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 124:1-5

1"Had it not been
the Lord who was on our side,"

Let Israel now say,

2"Had it not been
the Lord who was on our side

When men rose up against us,

3Then they would
have swallowed us alive,

When their anger was kindled
against us;

4Then the waters
would have engulfed us,

The stream would have swept
over our soul;

5Then the raging
waters would have swept over our soul."

124:1-5 This is a liturgical strophe related to the deliverance of national Israel from a foreign invader (i.e., "men rose
against us"). The exact historical setting is not stated.

The psalmist uses powerful imagery to convey YHWH's deliverance.

- He is on their side, Ps. 124:2

- the enemy would have swallowed Israel, Ps. 124:3a

- the enemy had their anger kindled against Israel, Ps. 124:3b

- the enemy, like a flood, would have engulfed Israel, Ps. 124:4-5

124:1 "Let Israel now say" This is a Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense. The
response would have been quoted at a national victory celebration (cf. Ps. 129:1).

124:3a This imagery of "swallowing" (BDB 118, KB 134) comes from

- the personification of the earth (i.e., death, Sheol cf. Exod. 15:12) swallowing the rebellious Levites
during the wilderness wandering period (cf. Num. 16:30,32; Deut. 11:6)

- the attack of a predatory animal (cf. Ps. 35:25; Prov. 1:12; Amos 2:16); this is stated specifically in Ps. 124:6b

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL

124:3b The imagery of anger as burning is first used in Gen. 39:19. Fire is used often imagery for

- judgment

- anger

- cleansing

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

124:4-5 The imagery of water/flood as life problems is recurrent in the OT (i.e., Job 22:11; 38:34; Ps. 32:6;
66:12; 69:2; 144:7; Isa. 43:2; Lam. 3:54). It is used of an invasion in Isa. 8:7-8 and Jer. 51:34, as it is in this Psalm. As
flood waters cover the land, so do invading armies. The other common metaphor for this was a locust infestation (i.e., Joel).

Whenever water is seen as an enemy of humanity, there may be an allusion to YHWH's defeat of
watery chaos (cf. Ps. 29:3,10; 74:12-17; 89:9-10; 93:3-4). This theme is part of YHWH as creator (cf. Ps. 124:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 124:6-8

6Blessed be the Lord,

Who has not given us to be
torn by their teeth.

7Our soul has
escaped as a bird out of the snare of the trapper;

The snare is broken and we
have escaped.

8Our help is in the
name of the Lord,

Who made heaven and earth.

124:6-8 YHWH is blessed (BDB 138, KB 159, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE) for His deliverance of
national Israel. The deliverance is characterized as

- escape from a predatory animal (i.e., Ps. 7:2)

- escape from a bird hunter/trapper (cf. Ps. 91:3; 119:110; Prov. 6:5)

124:7a "soul" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

124:7b One wonders if this line of poetry is meant to convey the destruction of the invading army.

124:8a The name stands for the person.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" of YHWH.

124:8b This is a set phrase (cf. Ps. 102:25; 121:2; 124:8; 134:3; 146:6) asserting the uniqueness of Israel's God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM
